newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Analysts welcome S.Africa dlr bond maturity, price.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome S.Africa dlr bond maturity, price.

text.p: South Africa's $300 million Yankee bond, launched on Friday, looked to be a success with the government getting a 10-year issue at a reasonably tight 195 basis points over equivalent U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.
South Africa's ability to raise a bond maturing in 2006 -- seven years after elections which will see Nelson Mandela step down as president -- was an encouraging sign.

"Two years ago we did a five-year global at 193 b.p. over. Now we are doing a 10-year at the same spread, which suggests we have at least come some way," said Nick Barnardt, strategic economist at BOE NatWest.
One banker in London said the bond looked like it was priced to sell, with spread talk ahead of the issue lower than the eventual launch spread.
However, Mike Brown, chief economist at stockbrokers Frankel Pollak in Johannesburg, said the authorities had got a good price: "Anything under 200 basis points was reasonable."
Dealers noted the Yankee spread was similar to South Africa's 10-year sterling bond early this year which came at 190 b.p. over.
Brown added recent issues had shown a useful increase in the maturity profile of South Africa's debt.
"They have got away from the five-year maturity which was fause there is a lot of debt maturing around 2001," he said.
Last month South Africa issued a 500 million mark issue at a 140 bspread.
The mark issue, together with the Yankee, will meet the government's budget target to raise offshore 2.5 billion rand of the forecast 1996/97 borrowing requirement of more than 40 billion rand.
Officials say South Africa has no problem funding its deficit domestically, but the state wants to raise funds overseas to improve and re-establish its bonds as benchmarks in foreign markets.
The country, which returned to the international capital markets in 1994 after years of isolation during the apartheid era, has also issued in yen.
South Africa is rated Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service and BB plus by Standard and poor's Corp, a rating which was affirmed on Thursday.

The Yankee issue has a pay date of October 17 which analysts said would provide a welcome capital injection as the authorities struggle with a weak rand which slipped to a seven-week low against the dollar this week.
